title: Prince Rupert and the Digby-coach royalist ciphers, 1645-46: Maurice to Rupert 1645 and BL Add MS 72438 ff. 9-10 (cryptiana #5, #6, unread); f. 107 deciphered with the f. 106 key

steps.what: Maurice's letter taken from the Warburton OCR; structure counted.
Known royalist key ranges compared with the 1645 figures.
Keys and originals located in BL Add MS 18980-82 and 72438; BL images offline since 2023, DECODE private.

DECODE cookie opens the private records; 115 records from Add MS 72438, 18982, 18983 listed with metadata (decode_records.tsv). No DOC transcriptions on any; Add MS 18980/18981 not on DECODE; no Maurice letter on DECODE.
f. 9r (R8623) and f. 10r-v (R8624) transcribed from the images: f. 9 letters 3-81 and words 100-343; f. 10 letters 1-99 and words 100-697; the two use different keys.
f. 25r (R8627) read: index of the keys taken in Digby's coach, numbered 80-139 with correspondents.

All 73 key records of Add MS 72438 screened by number range and structure from the images; most excluded by range (word series ending below 343, letter+digit codes, French/Latin/Weckherlin keys, 4-digit code).

Letter tables transcribed and applied to the letter runs of f. 9 and f. 10: key 118 Ormond-Rupert (R8655), key 123 King-Queen (R8687), key 125 Mr Browne (R8694), Digby-Walsingham (R8724), the 'To decypher speedily' key (R8744/R8745). All give gibberish.

Maurice 1645 tested against key 118 (Ormond-Rupert) letter table: '15 26 ... 13' = a m ... c, no sense; Tomokiyo's Nicholas-Rupert May 1645 key fragment (DECODE R8430/R8432 notes) gives no sense on Maurice or f. 9.

Add MS 18982 ff. 51-52 (R8433, 'Bristoll', non-decrypted) identified as Arthur Trevor to Rupert, Bristol 8 April 1645, with ~60 cipher groups of the same shape as Maurice's (letters <100, words 100+): a possible same-family key, not yet broken.
R8433 (Trevor to Rupert, Bristol [28] April 1645) cipher passages transcribed: 62 groups, 54 letter groups in 4 runs, 8 word groups.
Warburton iii OCR grepped for Trevor's April 1645 letter and the Molyneux/O'Neill passage; web search on the landing.
Homophonic annealing (en-1640s) on R8433's letter runs with 'chester'/'bristol' fixed on the 7-letter run and with no crib; box letter tables applied.
f. 104r (R8725) transcribed: 253 numeric groups + endorsement 347 313 364; no decipherment on the sheet despite DECODE 'Decrypted'.

f. 104 tested with letter tables 118, 123, 125, R8744 and the Parliament key R8741 (letters 10-72, nulls 1-9/73-75): nonsense. f. 107 (R8728) is a graphic cipher, so its key cannot apply to f. 9/f. 10.
f. 106 (R8727) two graphic alphabets transcribed; the lower one tested on f. 107 (R8728) against the interlinear gloss ('I hoped for some comfortable lynes ...').

f. 107 deciphered line by line with the f. 106 lower alphabet plus a few unlisted homophones (Ʈ=h, ɣ=r, 7=y, plain e, plain α=t): 129 words, 6 unread = 95.3%. A woman's letter to a royalist officer who got safe to the King; no names or date.

Write-up count: f107_reading.txt measured (129 tokens less the editorial '[one]' = 128 cipher words, 122 read = 95.3%); line 6 transcribed sign by sign and decoded with the f. 106 lower alphabet (f107_decode.py) for the reveal; all six documents measured for fraction_read.

outcome.method_basis: The only text obtained is f. 107 (R8728), deciphered 95.3% of words with the lower alphabet of the key sheet filed beside it (f. 106, R8727); the cryptiana items themselves (Maurice 1645, f. 9, f. 10) and f. 104 and R8433 are not solved, so the primary method describes a by-product of the search, not the targets as posed.
outcome.notes: Read in part only through f. 107, a letter found beside the targets in the same volume. The cryptiana items #5 and #6 remain unread: f. 9/f. 10 are May 1646, seven months after the coach keys were taken (Oct 1645), so their keys were probably never captured with them; Maurice's 'your cipher' is not in the volume or on DECODE.

parts.basis: 122 of 128 cipher words (95.3%) with the f. 106 lower alphabet, checked against the partial contemporary gloss; the six open words are a blot and writer slips (read bar met)

outcome.fraction_read_source: All six documents, cipher tokens, clear words excluded: maurice1645_groups.txt 93 groups, f9_groups.txt 152, f10_groups.txt 721, f104_groups.txt 256 (with the endorsement), trevor1645_transcription.txt 62 (--digits), f107_reading.txt 128 cipher words (129 with --drop-first, less the editorial '[one]'); total 1,412. Read: 122 words of f. 107 ([..?] conjectures counted unread); the numeric documents 0. 122/1412 = 0.086. f. 107 is counted in words, not signs, because no full sign-level transcription exists; counted in letters it would weigh about four times more, so the figure is a lower bound of the share of cipher material read, and the cryptiana items themselves stand at 0.

prior.where: f. 107 (R8728) carries a partial contemporary interlinear gloss (on the image, found before the attempt); nothing in print or on DECODE for any of the six documents

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
